correctness.rationale: The common absorbing basepoint is kept separate, and a nonzero monomial has uniquely reduced exponent coordinates with support surviving periodic reduction because d_i≥1. Supports multiply by union, so saturation forces precisely the coordinate-generated R_I. Group completion cancels the tails and gives the indicated product of cyclic groups; the orbital stabilizer axiom makes F precisely the inverse image of the identity of the quotient, hence a subgroup fiber under completion. Conversely every subgroup fiber obeys the axiom; equal cosets can be made equal in the monoid by first multiplying one representative by a lift in F, then multiplying both by the same sufficiently large product of period powers in F. This proves the quotient isomorphism as well as uniqueness, including I empty and periods 1. The inspected general splitting theorem applies to this finite pointed abelian monoid. Gaussian symmetry counts quotient dimension s by [k choose s]_p; splitting off the sphere and applying stable Hurewicz in degree one to connected BG gives precisely the displayed K₀ and K₁, including the merged 2-primary copies. For d=r−k, the central exponent drops by d(2r−d)/4 up to one unit from the floors: for 1≤d≤r/2 the drop is at least 3rd/8−1, and for d>r/2 it is at least 3r²/16−1. With the stated Gaussian bounds this makes the lower layers o(a_r). The centered Gaussian terms are summably bounded at fixed prime, and their product ratio tends to Q_p^−1 at each fixed offset, giving the two parity constants. The exact symmetry identity for T then gives the limit 1/2. An independently enumerated unequal-period case with r=2, d=(1,2), p=(2,1) matched actual pair sets, with counts 1,2,1,2 by support.
residual_risks: The frozen program's Gaussian portion checks aggregate R and T, not an independently enumerated full quotient-dimension table in the larger tested ranks. The symbolic Gaussian count proves each multiplicity.
Bounded pair-set comparisons do not establish the arbitrary-parameter theorem or the limits.

evidence: Sarazola–Shapiro–Zakharevich's theorem covers the splitting for every finite abelian monoid, and their one-generator calculation already yields the divisor-indexed wedges for the periodic factor. Weissmann's distinguishable-monoid isomorphism to the product of maximal-subgroup Burnside rings applies on the commutative side. Kousidis covers the raw subspace growth for every prime power.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Credit those wider results at their full scope. The first takes unevaluated orbital pairs as input, the second concerns the Burnside ring instead of stable summands, and the third concerns one vector-space dimension at a time rather than the support-weighted family.

checked_sources: Prior general splitting and Burnside statements
value.rationale: A product of periodic generators is a natural test of the general wedge theorem: it retains genuinely mixed subgroups and shows that increasing all preperiods has no effect on the invariant. Exact stable multiplicities and integral K₁ give usable information beyond additive orbit counts, while the transferred asymptotic measures a concrete superpolynomial K₀ rank versus monoid size. The value is in their joint evaluation for the family, not in rederiving classical Gaussian limits in isolation.
residual_risks: No higher stable homotopy group evaluations, mixed-relation classification, or uniform prime limit is claimed.
